equity.level_reason: Prevalence by race/ethnicity, education, income, insurance and sexual orientation is reported and the Discussion frames disparities and stressors, but group values are only set side by side with no computed difference or ratio, so the cap at 2 applies.

view_issues: Summary says the highest e-cigarette prevalence was 'among smokers aged 18–24 years (9.3%)', but 9.3% is for all adults aged 18–24 in the Table; 'smokers' appears erroneous. 'Higher' claims rest on no stated test or criterion.
